text:
Priya: Heads up — BayLake POC kicks off tomorrow. Need a fast checklist for access: hosted API keys for app devs, Dedicated pool for perf tests, and private/VPC onboarding for security review. Also need RBAC invites + least-privilege guidance. Who can help?

Marco: I got this. Quick summary: hosted keys = immediate (self-serve), Dedicated pools = request reserved capacity (expect ~48–72h), Private/VPC = depends on customer infra — usually 1–2 weeks for network setup. For RBAC, use scoped roles + ephemeral keys for engineers.

Marco: Minimal role set I recommend for POCs:
- poc_viewer: read-only access to metrics + logs
- poc_developer: inference invoke + evals run + analytics read
- poc_admin: create pools / invite (only 1–2 people)
Keep most folks as poc_developer.

Marco: For CI / automated runs use a service account with token TTL and only the `inference:invoke` scope. Example ephemeral key mint (admin action):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/keys/ephemeral \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <ORG_ADMIN_TOKEN>' \n  -d '{"expires_in":3600,"scopes":["inference:invoke"],"pool":"dedicated:bayside-1"}'
```

Sam: Note on Dedicated pools: we need the pool spec (GPU type, concurrency) and an account owner to sign the reserved contract. Once requested, infra will provision and we will map the pool to the org and create the `dedicated:<pool-name>` claim so ephemeral keys can route there.

Alyssa: For guest consultants — do we create real workspace users or invite as external guests? Security team will ask.

Marco: External guests (short-term): invite as workspace guests + enforce SSO and 7-day TTL. For anything automated, create scoped service accounts instead of sharing user keys.

SecurityBot: Checklist reminder: enable audit logging, KMS for keys in Dedicated/Private, IP allowlist for VPC endpoints, and SAML group mapping for role sync. Link: https://redwood.example/docs/security-poc-checklist

Priya: Customer Qs: 1) Who can view API keys? 2) Can we restrict keys to only inference endpoints? 3) How do we prove we didn't exfiltrate data?

Sam: Answers: 1) Only org admins + audit logs record key creation. 2) Yes — scope tokens to `inference:invoke` and optionally `models:read`. 3) Enable audit logs + request/response sampling retained in the console; for Private you can point to customer-managed logging.

Marco: Additional operational notes:
- For Hosted API keys used in early dev, rotate every 24–72h for POC.
- Use `poc_developer` role for dev machines, `poc_viewer` for PMs.
- If BayLake needs on-prem isolation, start Private/VPC intake now — we'd need their CIDR and DNS settings.

DeployBot: Provision request created: ticket REDWOOD-POC-7892. Dedicated pool ETA ~60h. Owner: @Sam (Platform).

Alyssa: Perfect — I'm answering the security questionnaire with this. Can someone join a 10am sync to run through invites and create the initial service accounts?

Marco: I can join. Sending calendar invite to Priya, Alyssa, Sam.

Priya: Thanks all — will update the opportunity notes and add the checklist link. :thumbsup:
